script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SMALL-TOWN - DAY

A quaint village nestled in the heart of the countryside. Farmlands surround it on all sides. Sunlight streams through trees. Birds chirp.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

RACHEL (25, small-town girl with freckles and a gentle smile) sits at a table, staring at her laptop. Her expression is thoughtful, her fingers dancing over the keyboard.

RACHEL
(to herself)
Come on, Rach. You can do this.

JACK (35, local handyman with kind eyes and a strong jaw) enters, setting down a tray of coffees on the counter. He notices Rachel and approaches her table.

JACK
(smiling)
Morning, Rach. You look lost in thought.

RACHEL
(startled)
Oh, hey Jack. Yeah, just trying to figure out this... (gestures to laptop) freelance writing gig.

JACK
(sitting down opposite her)
What's the topic?

RACHEL
It's about finding beauty in small-town life. But I can't seem to put my thoughts into words.

Jack looks thoughtful, then leans back and steeples his fingers.

JACK
Well, what makes your small town beautiful to you?

RACHEL
(pausing)
I guess it's the simplicity of it all. The way everyone knows each other. The quietness. The fresh air. The way the sunsets paint the sky every evening.

Jack nods, sipping his coffee.

JACK
That's a good start. Why don't you write about those things?

RACHEL
(brightening)
Really? You think so?

JACK
Absolutely. Sometimes the simplest things are the most profound.

INT. RACHEL'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Rachel sits at her desk, laptop open, as the sun sets outside her window. Jack's words echo in her mind. She begins to type.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The next day, Jack finds Rachel deep in thought, her laptop open in front of her.

JACK
(smiling)
You seem focused today, Rach.

RACHEL
(looking up)
I am. Jack, I think I've found my inspiration.

JACK
(leaning against the counter)
That's great news! What's your topic now?

RACHEL
I'm writing about the simple joys of small-town life. The warmth of the community. The tranquility of the countryside. The beauty of the changing seasons.

Jack's face lights up.

JACK
That's perfect. Write from the heart, Rach. I believe in you.

INT. RACHEL'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Rachel types away at her laptop, the only light in the room coming from the screen. As she writes, she reflects on the beauty of her small town.

EXT. SMALL-TOWN - DAY

The seasons change, but Rachel continues to write, drawing inspiration from her surroundings. Jack supports her every step of the way, encouraging her to share her words with the world.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

One day, as Rachel finishes the final draft of her article, Jack surprises her with a local newspaper.

JACK
(excitedly)
Look what I found, Rach!

Rachel scans the front page and gasps. Her article, "The Simple Joys of Small-Town Life," is featured in the local paper. Tears well up in her eyes as she reads the words she's written.

RACHEL
(whispering)
I did it.

Jack grins, proud of his friend.

JACK
You did, Rach. And I know it's just the beginning.

FADE OUT.
